# Adjudication Task — Chapter 501

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃501화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“언젭니까?”
  6|
  7|제갈풍과 헤어진 후 돌아가는 길, 내가 불현듯 던진 물음에 진위경이 나직하게 대답했다.
  8|
  9|“달포 후. 하남성 숭산(嵩山).”
 10|
 11|“숭산…….”
 12|
 13|무림의 태산북두인 소림사가 위치한 바로 그곳이다.
 14|
 15|불과 석 달 전. 천하 무림의 대연회라 할 수 있는 성라대연(星羅大宴)이 시작되고 암천에 의해 피바람이 불어닥친 그 자리에, 신(新) 무림맹이 탄생하는 것이다.
 16|
 17|숭산이라는 장소. 그리고 소림사가 지닌 상징성을 생각해 본다면, 장장 오십여 년 만에 부활하는 무림맹의 출발선으로는 적격인 셈이다.
 18|
 19|그나저나 겨우 달포밖에 남지 않았다는 건…….
 20|
 21|“이미 정해져 있었군요. 사천에 오셨을 때부터.”
 22|
 23|그러나 내 예상과는 반대로, 진위경은 작게 고개를 내저어 보였다.
 24|
 25|“아닙니까?”
 26|
 27|“위팽이 왜 때마침 하남에 있었다고 생각하느냐?”
 28|
 29|“그럼 위 대협이 온 이유가…….”
 30|
 31|“진룡대는 본가 제일의 정예다. 그중 절반이나 되는 인원을 고작 짐꾼으로 쓰기 위해 불러오는 것은 소가주로서 허락하지 않는다. 설령 옮기고자 하는 것이 천자의 옥새(玉璽)라 해도.”
 32|
 33|“예상보다 앞당겨진 거군요.”
 34|
 35|“암천의 행보가 생각했던 것 이상으로 거칠고 빨랐다. 사천혈사가 결정적이었지.”
 36|
 37|앞서가는 적을 따라잡기 위해서는 뛰어야 한다.
 38|
 39|소림사에 휘몰아친 피바람은 사천으로 나아갔고, 이제는 호북에까지 이르렀다. 하남의 수뇌부는 선택해야 했다.
 40|
 41|“천하 무림을 한 울타리에 묶는 것은 결코 쉬운 일이 아니다. 하지만 그분들께서도 마침내 결심을 내린 듯싶구나.”
 42|
 43|조용한 목소리로 뇌까린 진위경이 품에서 봉첩(封牒)을 꺼내 내밀었다.
 44|
 45|“이건.”
 46|
 47|“위팽이 하남에서 가져온 서신이다.”
 48|
 49|“하남이라면, 역시 무림맹에서 보낸 겁니까?”
 50|
 51|“짐작하고 있었구나.”
 52|
 53|“그럴 것 같더라고요. 아까 제갈 대협한테 주는 거 보고 알았어요.”
 54|
 55|척 봐도 보통의 서신과는 외관부터가 다르다.
 56|
 57|하지만 이 서신을 더욱 특별하게 만드는 것은, 겉면에 용사비등한 필체로 적힌 무림맹(武林盟)이라는 세 글자였다.
 58|
 59|“막내 너도 직접 읽어 보거라.”
 60|
 61|“이미 읽고 있으니까 말 시키지 마세요. 집중 안 돼요.”
 62|
 63|“……아앗, 으응.”
 64|
 65|나는 시무룩해하는 진위경을 뒤로하고 펼친 서신을 빠르게 훑어내렸다.
 66|
 67|천하 무림에 고하노라, 라는 문장으로 시작된 서신의 내용은 짧고 강렬했다. 그래서인지 세 줄 요약도 쉬웠다.
 68|
 69|
 70|
 71|1. 야야, 암천 썰 푼다. 이거 진짜 미친놈들이니까 잘 들어 봐.
 72|
 73|2. 정마대전 PTSD 알지? 이거 무슨 수를 써서라도 막자.
 74|
 75|3. 숭산 어딘지 모르는 호구 없재? 몇 월 며칠까지 모여라. 안 오는 새끼 암천.
 76|
 77|
 78|
 79|“…….”
 80|
 81|세 줄 요약해 놓고 보니까 되게 없어 보이네.
 82|
 83|당연하지만, 서신에 이렇게 쓰여 있지는 않았다.
 84|
 85|누군지 모르는 서예가가 거침없이 써 내려간 필체는 구름 같았고, 문장 하나하나와 그에 담긴 감정은 장엄하며 심금을 울렸다.
 86|
 87|개인적으로 암천의 천주라는 놈에게 보여 주고 싶을 정도다.
 88|
 89|‘이거 보면 천주도 무림맹 가입하겠다.’
 90|
 91|천주가 무림맹에 가입하면 모두가 행복한 해피 엔딩을 맞이할 수 있을 텐데, 그럴 가능성이 혁무진 귓밥만큼도 존재하지 않는다는 게 안타까울 뿐이다.
 92|
 93|“어쨌건, 이제 곧 무림맹이 탄생하겠군요.”
 94|
 95|“달포 뒤. 천하 무림이 무림맹의 깃발 아래 모일 것이다.”
 96|
 97|잠시 생각하던 진위경이 한마디를 덧붙였다.
 98|
 99|“천하 무림이 아니라, 중원의 정파 무림이라고 해야겠군.”
100|
101|진위경이 덧붙인 저 말의 의미를, 나는 이미 알고 있다.
102|
103|‘확실히…… 정파가 천하 무림 그 자체라고 하기에는 무리가 있지.’
104|
105|작금 천하 무림의 패자는 두말할 것 없이 구파일방과 오대세가를 위시한 정파다.
106|
107|그러나 과거 정마대전에서 살아남아 승자가 된 것은 정파뿐만이 아니었다.
108|
109|“사파(邪派).”
110|
111|내 입술 사이로 흘러나온 중얼거림에 진위경이 고개를 끄덕였다.
112|
113|“그래, 그들을 배제해서는 안 된다.”
114|
115|천하라는 어항에는 한 색깔의 물고기만 살아가는 것이 아니다.
116|
117|정파에 비하면 미력하나 자신들만의 영역을 구축한 사파가 있고, 밤거리를 지배하는 흑도가 포함되어 있다.
118|
119|‘처음에는 그렇게 사마외도 척결을 부르짖으면서 왜 저런 놈들을 남겨 뒀나 했는데.’
120|
121|모든 일에는 이유가 있는 법.
122|
123|지금까지 명맥을 이어 가고 있는 사파 세력은 정마대전 당시 정파의 편에 섰기 때문에 살아남을 수 있었다.
124|
125|문제는 그들의 선택이 단순한 선의가 아니었다는 점이다.
126|
127|“현존하는 중원의 사파 세력이 왜 정파 무림의 편에 섰는지, 혹 알고 있느냐?”
128|
129|“제가 지난 일 년 사이 누구와 함께 있었는지 잊으신 건 아니죠?”
130|
131|“적 대협께서 말씀해 주셨구나.”
132|
133|“이것저것 많이 주워들었죠.”
134|
135|옛말에 초록은 동색이고, 가재는 게 편이라고 했다.
136|
137|정마대전 당시 마교가 청해를 넘어 중원을 향해 들이닥치자, 사파는 교주님 만세를 부르짖으며 재빨리 합류했다.
138|
139|그만큼 마교의 기세가 엄청난 것도 있었지만 나름대로 동류라 할 수 있는 마교가 천하 무림의 주인이 되길 원했던 것이다.
140|
141|그러나 천하의 중심부라 할 수 있는 중원(中元)에 자리 잡고 있던 사파 무림인들은 사정이 달랐다.
142|
143|
144|
145|‘정파에 안 붙으면 당장 중원을 빠져나가기도 전에 척살 당할 텐데, 제깟 놈들이 이쪽에 안 붙고 배겨?’
146|
147|
148|
149|언젠가 적천강이 코웃음 치며 했던 그 말은 당시 중원의 사파인들에게 정확히 해당되는 현실이었다.
150|
151|“거의 울며 만두 먹기 식이었다고 하던데요.”
152|
153|“나 역시 그 시대에 살았던 건 아니지만, 확인해 본 바에 의하면 사실이다.”
154|
155|“확인?”
156|
157|“네가 사천에 떠난 뒤 하남에 남아 옛 자료를 찾아보는 과정에서 수많은 기록을 발견할 수 있었다. 사파에 관련된 기록도 그중 하나였고.”
158|
159|평화가 찾아오자 무림맹은 해산되었지만, 정마대전을 겪은 사람들의 기억과 당시의 상황을 고스란히 담은 기록은 남아 있었다.
160|
161|생각해 보면 당연한 일이다. 장구한 무림의 역사에서 오십여 년이라는 시간은 ‘고작’ 반세기에 불과하니까.
162|
163|“기록에 뭐라고 적혀 있었는데요?”
164|
165|“어떨 것 같으냐?”
166|
167|“어느 정도 예상이 되긴 하네요. 들은 이야기들이 있어서.”
168|
169|“적 대협께서 네게 정확히 어떤 이야기를 해 주셨는지는 모르나, 아마 대부분 사실일 것이다.”
170|
171|“……그게 사실이면 좀 골 때리는데.”
172|
173|정마대전의 시작과 동시에 중후반에 접어들기까지, 정파에 합류한 사파 무림인들은 끊임없는 배신을 반복했다.
174|
175|당시 무림맹 수뇌부가 정파 내부의 사파를 모조리 뽑아내는 삭초제근(削草除根)까지 논의했다는 적천강의 말을 생각하면 심각한 수준이었던 건 확실해 보인다.
176|
177|“그래도 나중에는 열심히 싸웠다면서요?”
178|
179|“처음과 달리 승패를 알 수 없게 되었으니까. 천면호리 송 대협이 이끄는 은영각(隱影閣)의 철통같은 감시도 있었고, 수뇌부의 분위기가 심상치 않음을 감지한 사파 무림 내부에서 자체적으로 꼬리를 잘라 냈다는 기록이 있다.”
180|
181|정파라고 무조건 정의로운 것은 아니고, 사파라고 아주 악질들만 모여 있는 것도 아니다.
182|
183|하지만 정파와 달리 사파는 스스럼없이 꼬리를 잘라 낼 수 있는 행동력과 잔혹함이 있었다.
184|
185|마교의 간자라고 의심이 가는 순간 가차 없이 멱부터 따고 본 것이다.
186|
187|“결국 꼬리를 잘라 낸 몸통은 살아남았고, 정파에 협조하여 승자가 되었지.”
188|
189|사파의 잔존 세력은 그렇게 정파라는 거목의 그늘서 명맥을 이어 갈 수 있었지만, 당연하게도 전과 같은 위세를 과시할 수는 없었다.
190|
191|가뜩이나 이미지가 지저분한데 마교에 붙어먹은 전력이 셀 수 없이 많았기 때문이었다.
192|
193|그나마 무림맹 수뇌부 측에서 어느 정도 공로와 권리를 인정해 줬기에 망정이지, 아니었다면 사마외도를 부르짖는 골수 의협들에게 끌려나가 오체분시 당했을 것이라는 게 중론이었다.
194|
195|종전 후에 사파를 향했던 혐오의 시선은 유구한 전통처럼 아직도 계속되고 있었다.
196|
197|여기까지는 그다지 크게 문제 될 게 없었지만, 지금부터는 얘기가 다르다.
198|
199|“걔들도 함께 데리고 싸워야 하잖아요.”
200|
201|“그래. 무림맹이 아니라면 암천의 편에 설 테니까.”
202|
203|“품에 안자니 찝찝한데요.”
204|
205|“전장에서 등을 맡기기에는 싫은 상대지. 전례도 있거니와 종전 후 논공행상에 대한 불만이 수십 년간 쌓여 있을 테니까.”
206|
207|“차라리 중립을 지키라고 한다면…….”
208|
209|“만약 무림맹이 패색이 짙다고 치자. 막내 네가 사파의 무림인이라면 어쩌겠느냐?”
210|
211|“……음.”
212|
213|저렇게 대놓고 물어보니까 뭐라 할 말이 없네. 입맛을 다신 내가 입을 열었다.
214|
215|“여기서 이런 말 하긴 뭐한데, 암천에 붙어야죠.”
216|
217|“이유는?”
218|
219|“무림맹이 이기면 본전이지만, 말하신 대로면 이미 승부의 저울은 기울었고 암천이 중원 무림의 주인이 될 상황이잖아요.”
220|
221|“그렇지.”
222|
223|“암천이 어떤 놈들인데 사파를 가만히 두겠습니까. 중립 지켰다고 칭찬하는 것보다 중요할 때 안 도왔으니 괘씸하다며 싸그리 죽여 버릴 놈들이죠.”
224|
225|“정확히 맞췄다. 그래서 사파가 계륵(鷄肋)인 것이다.”
226|
227|계륵. 상당히 적절한 표현이다.
228|
229|별로 득이 되진 않지만, 버리기에는 아깝다. 함께 싸우자니 찝찝하고 버리면 암천이 고스란히 주워 이쪽을 향해 던질 것이다.
230|
231|닭 뼈가 아무리 말랑해도 결국 뼈. 맞게 되면 제법 아프겠지.
232|
233|그렇다면 결국…….
234|
235|“하남에서도 이미 그쪽으로 서신을 보냈겠군요.”
236|
237|진위경이 작게 고개를 끄덕였다.
238|
239|“틀림없다. 굳이 둘 중 하나를 택해야 한다면, 사파 무림은 반드시 우리 쪽으로 끌어들여야 해.”
240|
241|사파는 계륵치고는 살점이 많이 붙어 있는 편이다.
242|
243|당장 해 떨어지면 뒷골목에 어슬렁거리는 흑도 칼잡이들도 사파에 속하는데, 지금은 삼류 칼잡이 하나가 아쉬울 때 아닌가.
244|
245|무엇보다 가까이 두고 목줄을 잡아채는 게 낫지, 아예 암천에 붙는 건 너무 큰 손해…….
246|
247|‘그런데 잠깐. 흑도?’
248|
249|나는 문득 떠오른 기억에 눈살을 찌푸렸다.
250|
251|“왜 그러느냐?”
252|
253|“아니, 얼마 전에 들은 게 기억나서요. 이번 수신룡에 관한 일로 호북성의 흑도를 흉수로 몰아서 싹 날려 보내지 않았습니까?”
254|
255|“그랬지.”
256|
257|“……그럼 사파 애들이 기분 나빠할 것 같은데요. 결국 우리가 관부의 제안을 받아들여서 자기네 식구 족친 거잖아요.”
258|

“The Jin Dragon Squad is our family’s finest fighting force. As the Lesser Family Head, I would never summon half its members merely to serve as porters, even if they were carrying the Son of Heaven’s jade seal.”

[P16]
“So the date was moved up.”

[P17]
“Dark Heaven moved more aggressively, and faster, than we expected. The Sichuan Blood Tragedy was decisive.”

[P18]
To catch an enemy who was ahead of you, you had to run.

[P19]
The storm of blood that had swept through Shaolin Temple had spread to Sichuan and now reached Hubei. The leaders in Henan had to make a choice.

[P20]
“Bringing the Murim under Heaven together is no easy task. But it seems they have finally made up their minds.”

[P21]
Jin Wikyung took a sealed dispatch from inside his robes and held it out.

[P22]
“What’s this?”

[P23]
“A letter Wipeng brought from Henan.”

[P24]
“From Henan? Did the Murim Alliance send it?”

[P25]
“You guessed.”

[P26]
“I thought so. I saw you give one to Sir Zhuge earlier.”

[P27]
Even at a glance, it looked nothing like an ordinary letter.

[P28]
But what made it special were the three characters written across its face in a bold, soaring hand:

[P29]
**Murim Alliance.**

[P30]
“Read it yourself, youngest.”

[P31]
“I’m already reading it, so stop talking. I can’t concentrate.”

[P32]
“…Oh. Right.”

[P33]
Leaving Jin Wikyung looking dejected, I unfolded the letter and skimmed it.

[P34]
It began, *To the Murim under Heaven,* and was short and forceful. That made it easy to sum up in three lines.

[P35]
1. Hey, let me tell you about Dark Heaven. These guys are seriously fucking crazy, so listen up.

[P36]
2. You remember the Great Faction War PTSD? Let’s stop this by any means necessary.

[P37]
3. Any dumbasses who don’t know where Mount Song is? Be there by the stated date. Anyone who doesn’t show up is Dark Heaven.

[P38]
“…”

[P39]
Put that way, it sounded pretty pathetic.

[P40]
Of course, that was not what the letter actually said.

[P41]
Some unknown calligrapher’s bold strokes flowed like clouds. Every sentence was solemn, charged with feeling, and deeply moving.

[P42]
Personally, I almost wanted to show it to that bastard, the Lord of Heaven.

[P43]
*If he saw this, even the Lord of Heaven might join the Murim Alliance.*

[P44]
Then everyone could have a happy ending. Unfortunately, the chance of that happening was smaller than the amount of earwax in Hyuk Mujin’s ear.

[P45]
“In any case, the Murim Alliance will be born soon.”

[P46]
“In a month, the Murim under Heaven will gather beneath its banner.”

[P47]
After a moment’s thought, Jin Wikyung added, “Not the Murim under Heaven. I should say the orthodox Murim of the Central Plains.”

[P48]
I knew what he meant.

[P49]
*Right… It’s a stretch to call the orthodox faction the whole Murim under Heaven.*

[P50]
The orthodox faction, led by the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families, was unquestionably the dominant force in the Murim today.

[P51]
But it had not been the only side to survive the Great Faction War and emerge victorious.

[P52]
“The unorthodox faction.”

[P53]
Jin Wikyung nodded at my mutter.

[P54]
“Yes. We cannot leave them out.”

[P55]
The fishbowl called the world held more than one color of fish.

[P56]
The unorthodox faction was weak compared to the orthodox faction, but it had carved out territories of its own. It also included the dark-path figures who ruled the streets at night.

[P57]
*At first, I wondered why the orthodox faction kept shouting about wiping out demonic, heterodox arts but left those people alive.*

[P58]
There was a reason for everything.

[P59]
The unorthodox forces still around today had survived because they sided with the orthodox faction during the Great Faction War.

[P60]
The trouble was, they had not done it out of goodwill.

[P61]
“Do you know why the unorthodox forces now active in the Central Plains sided with the orthodox Murim?”

[P62]
“You haven’t forgotten who I’ve spent the past year with, have you?”

[P63]
“Great Hero Jeok told you.”

[P64]
“I picked up quite a bit.”

[P65]
As the old saying went, green went with green, and crayfish took the crab’s side.

[P66]
When the Demonic Cult crossed Qinghai and surged toward the Central Plains, the unorthodox faction had quickly joined them, shouting, “Long live the Cult Leader!”

[P67]
The Demonic Cult’s momentum was overwhelming, but the unorthodox faction also wanted people they saw as their own kind to rule the Murim under Heaven.

[P68]
For unorthodox martial artists already living in the Central Plains, though, things were different.

[P69]
*If they didn’t side with the orthodox faction, they’d be hunted down before they even got out of the Central Plains. You think those bastards could afford not to join us?*

[P70]
Jeok Cheongang had once said that with a snort. For the unorthodox martial artists of the Central Plains, it had been the plain truth.

[P71]
“I heard they were practically eating dumplings through their tears.”

[P72]
“I did not live through that era either, but what I found confirms it.”

[P73]
“What you found?”

[P74]
“After you left for Sichuan, I stayed in Henan and searched the old archives. There were countless records, including ones about the unorthodox faction.”

[P75]
The Murim Alliance had disbanded when peace returned, but the memories of those who had lived through the Great Faction War—and records of what had happened—remained.

[P76]
That made sense. In the long history of the Murim, fifty years was *only* half a century.

[P77]
“What did the records say?”

[P78]
“What do you think?”

[P79]
“I can guess. I’ve heard a few stories.”

[P80]
“I do not know exactly what Great Hero Jeok told you, but most of it was probably true.”

[P81]
“…Then it’s pretty damn bad.”

[P82]
From the start of the Great Faction War well into its middle and later stages, the unorthodox martial artists who joined the orthodox faction betrayed them again and again.

[P83]
Jeok Cheongang had told me the Murim Alliance’s leaders had even discussed rooting out every unorthodox martial artist in their ranks. Things must have been serious.

[P84]
“But I heard they fought hard later on.”

[P85]
“Unlike at the beginning, neither side’s victory was certain. The Hidden Shadow Pavilion, led by Sir Song, the Thousand-Faced Fox, also kept them under close watch. And according to the records, the unorthodox martial artists sensed the leadership’s mood changing and began cutting off their own tails.”

[P86]
Not everyone in the orthodox faction was righteous, and not everyone in the unorthodox faction was a monster.

[P87]
But the unorthodox faction had the will and the cruelty to cut off its own tail without hesitation.

[P88]
The moment they suspected someone of being a Demonic Cult spy, they slit his throat.

[P89]
“In the end, the body survived without its tail. By cooperating with the orthodox faction, it shared in the victory.”

[P90]
The surviving unorthodox forces carried on in the shade of the great tree that was the orthodox faction. Naturally, they could no longer wield the influence they once had.

[P91]
Their reputation had been bad enough to begin with, and there had been countless instances of them siding with the Demonic Cult.

[P92]
Most people agreed that if the Murim Alliance’s leaders had not acknowledged at least some of their contributions and rights, hardline heroes calling for the extermination of demonic and heterodox elements would have dragged them out and torn them limb from limb.

[P93]
The contempt directed at the unorthodox faction after the war had endured like an ancient tradition.

[P94]
That alone was not a serious problem. What came next was.

[P95]
“We need them to fight alongside us.”

[P96]
“Yes. If they do not join the Murim Alliance, they will side with Dark Heaven.”

[P97]
“I don’t like the thought of bringing them into the fold.”

[P98]
“They are not people I would want to trust with my back on a battlefield. There is the precedent, and they must have spent decades resenting how honors and rewards were divided after the war.”

[P99]
“What if we tell them to stay neutral?”

[P100]
“Suppose the Murim Alliance looks certain to lose. What would you do if you were an unorthodox martial artist, youngest?”

[P101]
“…Hmm.”

[P102]
Put that bluntly, I had no answer. I smacked my lips before speaking.

[P103]
“I hate to say it, but I’d side with Dark Heaven.”

[P104]
“Why?”

[P105]
“If the Murim Alliance wins, they’re no better off than before. But in your scenario, the scales have already tipped. Dark Heaven is about to rule the Murim of the Central Plains.”

[P106]
“Exactly.”

[P107]
“And what kind of people are Dark Heaven? They wouldn’t leave the unorthodox faction alone. They wouldn’t praise them for staying neutral—they’d be furious they hadn’t helped when it mattered and kill every last one of them.”

[P108]
“Precisely. That is why the unorthodox faction is a chicken rib.”

[P109]
A chicken rib. That was a good way to put it.

[P110]
There was not much to gain from it, but throwing it away would be a waste. Fighting beside them felt risky, but if we cast them off, Dark Heaven would pick them up and throw them straight back at us.

[P111]
However soft a chicken bone might be, it was still a bone. Getting hit with one would hurt.

[P112]
Which meant…

[P113]
“Henan has already sent them a letter too, hasn’t it?”

[P114]
Jin Wikyung gave a small nod.

[P115]
“Without a doubt. If they must choose one side, we have to bring the unorthodox Murim over to ours.”

[P116]
For a chicken rib, the unorthodox faction had plenty of meat on it.

[P117]
Even the dark-path swordsmen who wandered the back alleys after sunset belonged to it. Right now, we could use even one Third Rate swordsman.

[P118]
Besides, it was better to keep them close enough to yank their leash than to let them join Dark Heaven. That would cost us far too much—

[P119]
*Wait. Dark-path figures?*

[P120]
Something came back to me, and I frowned.

[P121]
“What is it?”

[P122]
“I just remembered something I heard recently. Over the Water God Dragon incident, didn’t we blame the dark-path figures in Hubei Province and wipe them out?”

[P123]
“We did.”

[P124]
“…Then the unorthodox faction might not be happy. We accepted the government’s proposal and went after their own people.”

[P125]
It was a bad look. They might even reject the Murim Alliance’s offer of membership over it.

[P126]
Jin Wikyung, however, looked perfectly calm.

[P127]
“Two things are wrong with that.”

[P128]
“What?”

[P129]
“First, the unorthodox Murim has been fractured since the war ended. Those people were rivals, not family. We used this opportunity to uproot the unusually numerous dark-path figures in Hubei. Other unorthodox forces will move into the space they left. For them, it is a new opportunity.”

[P130]
“…!”

[P131]
“We have given them enough to feed on. They will be satisfied. And when they hear what happened in Hubei, they will understand that it was also a warning.”

[P132]
We had thrown them food and fastened a leash of fear around their necks.

[P133]
That was how the Murim Alliance tamed the hunting dog known as the unorthodox Murim.

[P134]
“And second, the government did not make the proposal for us to accept.”

[P135]
Jin Wikyung’s voice went dry.

[P136]
“We did. No—I made the proposal first.”

[P137]
“Oh.”

[P138]
“The government merely accepted it. That distinction matters a great deal.”

[P139]
“…The government agreed that easily?”

[P140]
“The Provincial Administration Commissioner of Hubei holds a post that can sway an entire province. But people know only that the new commissioner formerly served as an Assistant Provincial Administrator in Shanxi Province. They do not know he is a secret loyal retainer of Prince Shangshan.”

[P141]
I remembered our arrival in Hubei.

[P142]
The hostile looks from the people. Jin Wikyung speaking to the official who had surrounded the ferry landing with government soldiers.

[P143]
*“By the way, do you know a man surnamed Yi whose given name is Hongcheon?”*

[P144]
*“H-he was recently appointed Provincial Administration Commissioner. May I ask what your relationship with him is…?”*

[P145]
*“We’ve met a few times and shared a drink or two. I’ve helped him when he needed it.”*

[P146]
Jin Wikyung looked straight at me. His gaze was gentle, but a cold blade lay behind it.

[P147]
For an instant, I saw the strategist and politician in him. Then that look melted away.

[P148]
“Do not worry. Everything will work out.”

[P149]
Tap, tap.

[P150]
There was strength in the hand patting my shoulder. I studied him for a moment, then asked without warning,

[P151]
“What was the Family Head… No, what was Father like?”

[P152]
The faint smile on Jin Wikyung’s lips vanished.

[P153]
“We were having such a nice moment. Why bring up that man?”

[P154]
“As you know, I hurt my head back then. I don’t remember him very well.”

[P155]
“You don’t need to! Erase him from your mind! I’m your father!”

[P156]
“…”

[P157]
I knew he had grievances, but apparently there were more than I had realized.

[P158]
Jin Wikyung’s fist trembled, as if he were remembering the paperwork hell of those days.

[P159]
“But why do you ask?”

[P160]
“No reason. I was just thinking how lucky it is that you took charge of the family after Father disappeared.”

[P161]
“…Youngest. Please don’t cross the line.”

[P162]
I shrugged and turned away.

[P163]
Behind me, Jin Wikyung demanded to know where I was going while my hyung was still talking, and whether I loved him any less now. I answered without looking back.

[P164]
“You said it’s in a month. I’m going to get ready to leave.”

[P165]
It was time to leave Hubei behind.

[P166]
With the people who were by my side, and whom I wanted beside me in the days to come.

[P167]
“I think I’ve given you enough time by now… Don’t you?”

[P168]
My mutter disappeared beneath the surrounding noise.

[P169]
I scratched my chin and looked up at the dizzyingly high cliff.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.

[P147]

[P148]

[P149]

[P151]

[P152]

[P153]

[P154]

[P155]

[P156]

[P158]

[P159]

[P160]

[P161]

[P162]

[P163]

[P164]

[P165]

[P166]

[P167]

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

“Unlike at the beginning, neither side’s victory was certain. The Hidden Shadow Pavilion, led by Sir Song, the Thousand-Faced Fox, also kept them under close watch. And according to the records, the unorthodox martial artists sensed the leadership’s mood changing and began cutting off their own tails.”

[P86]
Not everyone in the orthodox faction was righteous, and not everyone in the unorthodox faction was a monster.

[P87]
But the unorthodox faction had the will and the cruelty to cut off its own tail without hesitation.

[P88]
The moment they suspected someone of being a Demonic Cult spy, they slit his throat.

[P89]
“In the end, the body survived without its tail. By cooperating with the orthodox faction, it shared in the victory.”

[P90]
The surviving unorthodox forces carried on in the shade of the great tree that was the orthodox faction. Naturally, they could no longer wield the influence they once had.

[P91]
Their reputation had been bad enough to begin with, and there had been countless instances of them siding with the Demonic Cult.

[P92]
Most people agreed that if the Murim Alliance’s leaders had not acknowledged at least some of their contributions and rights, hardline heroes calling for the extermination of demonic and heterodox elements would have dragged them out and torn them limb from limb.

[P93]
The contempt directed at the unorthodox faction after the war had endured like an ancient tradition.

[P94]
That alone was not a serious problem. What came next was.

[P95]
“We need them to fight alongside us.”

[P96]
“Yes. If they do not join the Murim Alliance, they will side with Dark Heaven.”

[P97]
“I don’t like the thought of bringing them into the fold.”

[P98]
“They are not people I would want to trust with my back on a battlefield. There is the precedent, and they must have spent decades resenting how honors and rewards were divided after the war.”

[P99]
“What if we tell them to stay neutral?”

[P100]
“Suppose the Murim Alliance looks certain to lose. What would you do if you were an unorthodox martial artist, youngest?”

[P101]
“…Hmm.”

[P102]
Put that bluntly, I had no answer. I smacked my lips before speaking.

[P103]
“I hate to say it, but I’d side with Dark Heaven.”

[P104]
“Why?”

[P105]
“If the Murim Alliance wins, they’re no better off than before. But in your scenario, the scales have already tipped. Dark Heaven is about to rule the Murim of the Central Plains.”

[P106]
“Exactly.”

[P107]
“And what kind of people are Dark Heaven? They wouldn’t leave the unorthodox faction alone. They wouldn’t praise them for staying neutral—they’d be furious they hadn’t helped when it mattered and kill every last one of them.”

[P108]
“Precisely. That is why the unorthodox faction is a chicken rib.”

[P109]
A chicken rib. That was a good way to put it.

[P110]
There was not much to gain from it, but throwing it away would be a waste. Fighting beside them felt risky, but if we cast them off, Dark Heaven would pick them up and throw them straight back at us.

[P111]
However soft a chicken bone might be, it was still a bone. Getting hit with one would hurt.

[P112]
Which meant…

[P113]
“Henan has already sent them a letter too, hasn’t it?”

[P114]
Jin Wikyung gave a small nod.

[P115]
“Without a doubt. If they must choose one side, we have to bring the unorthodox Murim over to ours.”

[P116]
For a chicken rib, the unorthodox faction had plenty of meat on it.

[P117]
Even the dark-path swordsmen who wandered the back alleys after sunset belonged to it. Right now, we could use even one Third Rate swordsman.

[P118]
Besides, it was better to keep them close enough to yank their leash than to let them join Dark Heaven. That would cost us far too much—

[P119]
*Wait. Dark-path figures?*

[P120]
Something came back to me, and I frowned.

[P121]
“What is it?”

[P122]
“I just remembered something I heard recently. Over the Water God Dragon incident, didn’t we blame the dark-path figures in Hubei Province and wipe them out?”

[P123]
“We did.”

[P124]
“…Then the unorthodox faction might not be happy. We accepted the government’s proposal and went after their own people.”

[P125]
It was a bad look. They might even reject the Murim Alliance’s offer of membership over it.

[P126]
Jin Wikyung, however, looked perfectly calm.

[P127]
“Two things are wrong with that.”

[P128]
“What?”

[P129]
“First, the unorthodox Murim has been fractured since the war ended. Those people were rivals, not family. We used this opportunity to uproot the unusually numerous dark-path figures in Hubei. Other unorthodox forces will move into the space they left. For them, it is a new opportunity.”

[P130]
“…!”

[P131]
“We have given them enough to feed on. They will be satisfied. And when they hear what happened in Hubei, they will understand that it was also a warning.”

[P132]
We had thrown them food and fastened a leash of fear around their necks.

[P133]
That was how the Murim Alliance tamed the hunting dog known as the unorthodox Murim.

[P134]
“And second, the government did not make the proposal for us to accept.”

[P135]
Jin Wikyung’s voice went dry.

[P136]
“We did. No—I made the proposal first.”

[P137]
“Oh.”

[P138]
“The government merely accepted it. That distinction matters a great deal.”

[P139]
“…The government agreed that easily?”

[P140]
“The Provincial Administration Commissioner of Hubei holds a post that can sway an entire province. But people know only that the new commissioner formerly served as an Assistant Provincial Administrator in Shanxi Province. They do not know he is a secret loyal retainer of Prince Shangshan.”

[P141]
I remembered our arrival in Hubei.

[P142]
The hostile looks from the people. Jin Wikyung speaking to the official who had surrounded the ferry landing with government soldiers.

[P143]
*“By the way, do you know a man surnamed Yi whose given name is Hongcheon?”*

[P144]
*“H-he was recently appointed Provincial Administration Commissioner. May I ask what your relationship with him is…?”*

[P145]
*“We’ve met a few times and shared a drink or two. I’ve helped him when he needed it.”*

[P146]
Jin Wikyung looked straight at me. His gaze was gentle, but a cold blade lay behind it.

[P147]
For an instant, I saw the strategist and politician in him. Then that look melted away.

[P148]
“Do not worry. Everything will work out.”

[P149]
Tap, tap.

[P150]
There was strength in the hand patting my shoulder. I studied him for a moment, then asked without warning,

[P151]
“What was the Family Head… No, what was Father like?”

[P152]
The faint smile on Jin Wikyung’s lips vanished.

[P153]
“We were having such a nice moment. Why bring up that man?”

[P154]
“As you know, I hurt my head back then. I don’t remember him very well.”

[P155]
“You don’t need to! Erase him from your mind! I’m your father!”

[P156]
“…”

[P157]
I knew he had grievances, but apparently there were more than I had realized.

[P158]
Jin Wikyung’s fist trembled, as if he were remembering the paperwork hell of those days.

[P159]
“But why do you ask?”

[P160]
“No reason. I was just thinking how lucky it is that you took charge of the family after Father disappeared.”

[P161]
“…Youngest. Please don’t cross the line.”

[P162]
I shrugged and turned away.

[P163]
Behind me, Jin Wikyung demanded to know where I was going while my hyung was still talking, and whether I loved him any less now. I answered without looking back.

[P164]
“You said it’s in a month. I’m going to get ready to leave.”

[P165]
It was time to leave Hubei behind.

[P166]
With the people who were by my side, and whom I wanted beside me in the days to come.

[P167]
“I think I’ve given you enough time by now… Don’t you?”

[P168]
My mutter disappeared beneath the surrounding noise.

[P169]
I scratched my chin and looked up at the dizzyingly high cliff.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
